clue.text: Outlaw pinching officer's breakfast?

indicators.note: to pinch is to grab and hold, so the outlaw's word holds the officer inside it

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
CO is the usual short form of commanding officer

explanation.surface: A criminal snatches a policeman's morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' reads as a bandit but is the verb, BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fried rashers are a typical example of a British morning meal, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Lord one encountered during party, rather thin on top

indicators.note: during means the pieces happen inside the word for party

parts.note: a bash is a party
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A peer meets someone at a party and notices they are going bald.
explanation.definitionFit: Baldish means slightly bald, losing hair on the crown.

clue.text: Language from China and France originally

indicators.note: originally, read as in an original way, means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tongue comes from two countries in its origins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' seems to mean 'at first' and so suggests first letters; here it means the words are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Canadian French is the variety of the Gallic tongue spoken in Quebec and elsewhere in Canada.

clue.text: Cnut upset with sea, the fool

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: King Cnut, defied by the tide, looks a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Cnut is the English king of the legend in which he commands the tide to turn back.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutcase is a crazy or foolish person, a colloquial term.

clue.text: Knox perhaps recalled receiving religious subjects

indicators.note: receiving means the reversed word takes another piece inside it
recalled, as in called back, means the word for Knox is read backwards

parts.note: John Knox, the Reformation preacher, is an example of a Scot
PI is short for pious, a crossword stand-in for religious

explanation.surface: A Scottish reformer's sermon themes on faith are remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: John Knox led the Scottish Reformation; 'perhaps' marks him as one example of a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Subjects and topics are both the matters under discussion: plain synonyms.

clue.text: Team leader determined to turn up fit for important fixture

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up reads the pieces from bottom to top, backwards
the leader of the word Team is its first letter

parts.note: determined means set, as in set on doing something
to fit is to match

explanation.surface: The captain is resolved to turn up fit for a big game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses T plus SET to TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is an international cricket or rugby game, the top fixture of a tour.

clue.text: Creature holed up in grotto perhaps

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the letters run backwards
holed means holed up, tucked inside the words grotto perhaps

explanation.surface: An animal is hiding in a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holed' and 'up' read as one phrase; 'up' reverses the letters OTTOP hidden in 'grotto perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A potto is a slow-moving African primate, a nocturnal animal.

clue.text: Place of altar in church, unusually clean

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of clean appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: The area around the altar in a church is remarkably tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' makes ANCEL from CLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar, reserved for clergy and choir.

clue.text: Right-leaning magazine's getting support from the left? That's one to watch

parts.note: The Spectator is a conservative British weekly
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A conservative weekly gets backing from the political left, which is worth watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support from the left' suggests political backing, but 'the left' is PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator sport is a game people enjoy viewing rather than playing.

clue.text: Prickly plant kid left behind

indicators.note: behind means the letter for left comes after the other piece

parts.note: to kid someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A child has been left behind among the thorny plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child but is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: The teasel is a spiny plant whose dried heads were used to raise the nap of cloth.

clue.text: Cough remedy workers swallowed in one part of England

indicators.note: the workers are swallowed, placed inside the county's letters

parts.note: LINCS is the short form of Lincolnshire, an English county
TU is a trade union, a body of workers

explanation.surface: Labourers in an English county take a medicine for their coughs.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincolnshire is a county in eastern England, shortened to LINCS.
explanation.definitionFit: A linctus is a syrupy medicine taken to soothe a cough.

clue.text: Long walk round various parts of Paris is extremely tiresome

indicators.note: round means the outer letters sit round the rearranged city name
extremely means the extreme letters, first and last, of tiresome
the parts of the word Paris are put in a varied order

explanation.surface: A long stroll round the sights of the French capital becomes exhausting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long walk' is the definition; the surface's 'Paris' is the city name used only for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to trudge wearily a long way; the noun is such a tiring walk.

clue.text: Home phone line cut off — where to ring for help?

parts.note: being home means being in

indicators.note: cut off means the line is removed from the word for phone

parts.note: to phone is to dial

explanation.surface: Your home phone has been disconnected, so where can you call for assistance?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to call centres, many of which are based in this country.
explanation.definitionFit: Many helplines are answered in call centres in that South Asian country, so it is where a caller rings.

clue.text: Needing to secure boat, helmsman audibly grouses

parts.note: to moor is to secure a boat at its berth

indicators.note: audibly means the word for helmsman is heard, giving a written form of the same sound

parts.note: a cox steers a rowing boat

explanation.surface: A steersman needs to tie up the vessel and complains about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouses' looks like a verb for complaining but is the plural noun for game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorcocks are male red grouse, the moorland game birds.

clue.text: In ideal hotel, water gushes warmer in the bathroom

indicators.note: water that gushes is thrown about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: In a perfect hotel the water pours out freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warmer' is a noun, a thing that warms.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated towel rail is a bathroom fitting that warms towels, so it is a warmer found there.

clue.text: Bird making loud cry, crossing Roman land

indicators.note: the cry goes across, around, the other piece, which sits inside

parts.note: a wail is a loud cry
terra is the Latin word for land

explanation.surface: A bird screams as it flies over Italian territory.
explanation.definitionFit: The water rail is a secretive marsh bird of the rail family.

clue.text: Film director beginning to feel embarrassed, having problem during

clue.text: Declare business has lost a million

indicators.note: lost means the word a is dropped from the word for business

parts.note: an affair is a matter or business

explanation.surface: A company announces it has lost a million.
explanation.walkthrough: 'business' reads as a firm; it is AFFAIR, which loses an A, then M is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm is to state firmly, to assert or declare.

clue.text: Make mark on English party

parts.note: a rave is a party

explanation.surface: An English party leaves its stamp.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave is to cut a design or letters into a surface, marking it.

clue.text: Trendies once having hot record by the Animals?

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
an EP is an extended-play record
cats are animals; the Animals were also a 1960s band

explanation.surface: Fashionable folk of the past have a hit single by a sixties rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: The Animals were a British band of the 1960s, a red herring for CATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hepcats was dated slang for hip, stylish people, so trendies of an earlier era.

clue.text: Corrupt behaviour new, say, in one US state

indicators.note: in means these pieces are placed inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky
to aver is to state or say

explanation.surface: Fresh dishonesty, so to speak, occurs in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Knavery is roguish or dishonest conduct, the behaviour of a knave.

clue.text: Warrior about to board ship

indicators.note: to board is to go into, so the short word goes inside the warrior's word

parts.note: a warrior is a fighter
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A soldier is about to climb aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to board' reads as 'soon to board'; in fact 'about' is RE and 'to board' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a cargo vessel, a kind of ship.

clue.text: Craftsman installing lift in bank

indicators.note: installing means the bank's word takes the lift's letter into it

parts.note: a tier is a bank, a row of seats or terraces
L is an abbreviation for lift

explanation.surface: A workman fits an elevator in a bank building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a financial building but is a tier or row.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiler is a tradesman who lays roof or floor tiles.

clue.text: Order tapas or spaghetti?

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so the letters of tapas are put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A diner decides between ordering small Spanish dishes or an Italian noodle dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads as asking a waiter; it is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is one example of the Italian dough food, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Island supplying holiday souvenir to everyone

parts.note: seaside rock is a hard stick of candy sold at British resorts like Blackpool
everyone means all

explanation.surface: An island sells keepsakes to all its visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Seaside rock is a British sweet: a stick of hard candy with the resort's name running through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockall is a tiny uninhabited Atlantic islet, also a British shipping-forecast area.

clue.text: France maybe gets the French to back a partnership of nations

indicators.note: to back means the French word goes at the back, after the others

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty alliance of member countries
le is French for the

explanation.surface: France joins an international alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'France' reads as the country; it is the writer Anatole France.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatole France was a French novelist, so he is an example of someone with that first name.

clue.text: Bird, oddly pretty, seen on loch

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters of the word pretty are taken

parts.note: RE means on, in the sense of concerning
L is the abbreviation for loch on maps

explanation.surface: A lovely bird is spotted on a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A petrel is a seabird, such as the storm petrel.

clue.text: Barbecued food cool at the end of the day

parts.note: SAT is short for Saturday, the day that ends the week
cool as an approving reply means yes, and ay is a dialect form of yes

explanation.surface: Grilled snacks are pleasant at the close of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool' is an approving yes, given here in its dialect form; 'the end of the day' means Saturday as the week's last day, not evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Satay is a South-East Asian dish of skewered meat grilled over coals.
